data_flows.protected_app: Browser → React Router → auth bootstrap → typed API client → Django session/CSRF → authentication → Company/Branch authorization → accepted DRF response → TanStack Query → authorized UI. Route guards are UX only; every protected endpoint authorizes again.
data_flows.login: Login page → GET /auth/csrf/ → CSRF cookie → POST /auth/login/ with Login ID/password and CSRF header → HttpOnly session cookie → GET /auth/me/ → first-password route or safe app route.
data_flows.first_password: Authenticated temporary session → restricted password route → CSRF-protected POST /auth/password/change/ → backend validation/lifecycle/audit/session response → GET /auth/me/ → protected app only when must_change_password is false.
data_flows.logout: User action → CSRF-protected POST /auth/logout/ → server invalidates session → clear auth state, query cache and selected Company/Branch state → login. On timeout, clear local sensitive state but do not claim server success; recheck /me on next load.
data_flows.session_expiry: Protected API returns 401 or bootstrap /me returns 401 → cancel requests and purge user-scoped cache → login/session-expired surface. 403 remains forbidden and must not trigger an auth loop.
data_flows.branch_filter: Fetch accepted Company-scoped Branch list → user selects an authorized Branch UUID → UI filter state → only endpoints that explicitly support the filter receive it → backend reauthorizes Company, Branch, action and object. Selection itself grants nothing.
data_flows.forbidden_uuid: UI/API receives direct Company or Branch UUID → backend scoped queryset/permission denies or hides it → safe forbidden/not-found UI. No client-side name/UUID matching or broad fallback.
data_flows.mock_to_real: Page field → P2-02 mapping → accepted endpoint serializer/source → runtime validation → scoped query → existing UI projection. If source is absent, preserve reference layout but mark/defer data; never infer from labels or local calculations.

security_rules: Django session remains HttpOnly/server-controlled; no long-lived auth token in localStorage/sessionStorage.
CSRF bootstrap and token header for every unsafe cookie request; use same-origin proxy or explicit allowlisted CORS/CSRF origins, never wildcard credentials.
Backend authorizes every request; UI routes, roles, Company/Branch selectors and hidden actions are not security controls.
Company accounts have one Company and no normal switcher; Platform identities remain a separate authorization path.
Branch choices are backend-filtered; direct UUID, cross-Company, stale membership and Branch assignment attempts are rejected server-side.
Query keys include authenticated identity and relevant Company/Branch; logout, 401, revocation and account change cancel/purge user-scoped state. Do not persist sensitive queries.
First-password restriction is enforced by backend and UI; direct route/API bypass fails.
Safe local redirects only; no open redirect. Distinguish 401 from 403/404.
Render backend text through React escaping; no unsafe HTML insertion; do not expose stack traces, password data or internal error details.
Carry request ID for support when available; never include credentials or sensitive bodies in logs/telemetry.
